facts.text: The study compressed [1̄23]-oriented single crystals and determined the CRSS for initial (111)[1̄01] slip as a function of temperature.
CRSS data outside the inertial and Portevin–Le Chatelier regimes were fitted with a thermal-activation equation to extrapolate the CRSS to 0 K.
Compression tests covered 9–1373 K at an engineering strain rate of 1 × 10^-4 s^-1.
Composition-dependent local lattice distortion, represented by mean-square atomic displacement, mediates the solid-solution resistance to dislocation glide.
Below about 60–77 K, reduced phonon drag permits inertial dislocation motion that dulls the thermally activated rise in CRSS.
The elevated-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier effect was attributed predominantly to Cottrell-type elastic pinning by diffusible Mn- and Fe-rich solute atmospheres.
CrFeNi showed no measurable high-temperature widening of dissociated partial dislocations, so the TEM evidence did not support substantial Suzuki segregation.
Cooling below room temperature increased the CRSS relative to the room-temperature value.
At 77 K, the CRSS was 1.85–2.53 times its room-temperature value.
The increase in CRSS became less steep below the alloy-specific critical temperature of approximately 60–77 K.
Heating into the diffusion-active regime increased CRSS above the intermediate-temperature baseline and produced serrated flow.
The high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier increment in CRSS was 1.5–11.4 MPa.
